title: Replay prober for structured-output config audit and rapid root-cause
creator: Sofia Li
description:
Problem: After several recent config rollouts (kernel-selection heuristics, quantization-profile updates and a per-model routing tweak), we've observed intermittent structured-output regressions where JSON fields are missing, coerced to null, or shifted (key renames) for a small but important subset of customer traffic. Current regression alerts flag dataset-level drift but do not give a fast, deterministic root-cause across config deltas and model variants.

Goal: Build a reproducible replay prober that can (1) replay representative requests against historically proxied model/config snapshots, (2) compute deterministic field-level diffs and probabilistic signal (regression likelihood), and (3) produce a ranked impact table with suspected root cause (model change / quantization / kernel). The probe should integrate with the evals harness, attach per-field diff artifacts to incidents, and be usable by SRE/PL/engineers during canary investigation.

Acceptance criteria:
- A runnable binary (or lambda) that can take a sample set ID and two environment snapshots (e.g., hosted:v1.19 with quant-profile A vs hosted:v1.20 with quant-profile B) and produce a signed JSON report containing per-field precision/recall/regression-signal and example traces (input + both outputs).
- Field-level delta scoring: percentage of records with missing/extra/typed-mismatch fields and a confidence score for likely config cause.
- Integration with CI: on rollout failures above threshold auto-create a ticket with attached report and suggested temporary mitigation (fallback model alias or quant-profile rollback).
- Dashboards and alert rules for prober-run regressions and heatmaps by customer cohort.

Design notes:
- Replay harness will sample customer traffic using our existing request sampling pipeline and store canonicalized inputs in bucketed archives (sample IDs). Canonicalization will include deterministic prompt normalization and a stable random seed for stochastic behaviors.
- To attribute cause we will run three axes: model-variant (v1/v2...), runtime-config (quantization/kernel flags), and routing-policy (region/capacity-tier). We then compute an attribution score using an ablation-style lattice (A/B/AB runs) and a simple causal score: delta_agreement * delta_magnitude / cost_penalty.
- Output artifacts: human-readable per-field diffs, a small set (<20) of representative golden/failed pairs, and a CSV for offline analysis. Reports must be signed and stored in S3 with retention policy 90 days.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Prototype replay runner (2 wks): basic runner that replays sample archives against two specified endpoints and stores paired outputs. (owner: Daniel)
2) Field differ and scorer (1 wk): implement canonicalizers and fieldwise scoring primitives (owner: Aisha Kapoor).
3) Attribution lattice and report generator (1 wk): compute attribution scores and assemble report artifacts (owner: Marco Diaz).
4) Integration and CI gating (1 wk): wire into rollout pipeline to run automatically on canary regressions > threshold, create tickets with links.
5) Dashboards & runbook (1 wk): Grafana dashboard and doc runbook for SRE and PM.

Trade-offs / open questions:
- Sampling volume vs cost: initial runs may reuse small 1k sample slices to limit GPU spend; later runs can scale on demand.
- Deterministic replay for non-deterministic models: we will use fixed temperature and token-level seeds where possible; for stochastic models we will run repeated samples and aggregate.
- Attribution may be noisy when multiple small changes are rolled together; consider enforcing smaller, atomic rollouts or delta-enforced rollouts.

Runbook snippets (for on-call):
- When structured-output alert triggers, run pre-populated prober with the sample ID attached to the alert: `prober run --sample 2026-02-24-cta --baseline snapshot:v1.19 --candidate snapshot:v1.20`
- If prober report indicates quantization-profile as primary cause, temporarily pin route to `quant-profile:legacy-8bit` and escalate to the runtime team.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to root-cause (MTTRC) for structured-output regressions reduced from current ~7h to <2h for P1 incidents.
- 90% of prober runs provide a top-1 suspected cause with confidence >0.6 for incidents above threshold.
- Number of false rollback suggestions below 5% in first quarter of rollout usage.
